The Night Before
11 PM. Fourteen hours to the final. You knock on Karan's door. He opens it with Veer's school drawing in his hand.
He drew me holding a trophy. I'm the tallest person in the picture. Taller than the stadium.
"Rathore's people will be at Veer's school tomorrow. I promise."
Make him believe it.
"Drop the catch if you have to. I'll cover it."
Give him permission.
Charter a jet. Bring Veer and his mother here tonight.
Out of Mehra's reach. In the stands tomorrow.
You're a good kid. I don't know if that's enough. I'll know at the seventeenth over.
At 4 AM a small plane lands at the city airport. At 6 AM a seven-year-old in pyjamas runs down the hotel corridor shouting "PAPA!"
...I don't know how to pay you back.
Yes I do. I'm going to catch everything tomorrow. Everything.
Can't sleep. Brought banana chips. Amma's last packet. Emergency only. This is an emergency.
I'm in the press box tomorrow. Flew in. Don't ask how much it cost.
Whatever happens at ball three, I'll write it true.
Hit one for Rajgarh.
My statement. Signed. Rathore has a copy. My father will never speak to me again.
Tomorrow, chaiwala, if you run yourself out, I'll kill you before Mehra can.
7:02 AM. Final day. Your phone lights up with a photo.
Papa at the stall, pouring chai. Two men in grey suits sitting on the bench. One of them is raising his glass to the camera.
"17th over. Ball 3. Your father makes excellent chai. — R"
Final day. Mehra's men are drinking Papa's chai. Ball three is waiting.
